claims.text: Equiatomic CrCoNi exhibits enhanced work hardening relative to equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Equiatomic CrCoNi exhibits delayed failure relative to equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
The enhanced work hardening and delayed failure of CrCoNi are caused by a magnetically tunable deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation.
The deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation is more pronounced in CrCoNi than in CrMnFeCoNi.
Mn or Fe in the quinary alloy disrupts magnetic ordering.
Disruption of magnetic ordering by Mn or Fe suppresses the FCC-to-HCP transformation in the quinary alloy.
The compared alloys can be prepared as single-phase FCC materials through thermomechanical processing.
Uniaxial tensile tests at matched temperature and strain rate, with and without an external magnetic field, provide a controlled comparison of the proposed magnetic contribution.
Magnetic interactions during deformation induce nucleation and growth of HCP phase from the FCC matrix.
Stronger magnetic interactions in CrCoNi promote its deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation.
The deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation increases work hardening and delays failure.
Under an applied magnetic field, CrCoNi will develop a higher HCP phase fraction than CrMnFeCoNi.
Under an applied magnetic field, CrCoNi will show a higher strain-hardening rate than CrMnFeCoNi.
Under an applied magnetic field, CrCoNi will show delayed necking relative to CrMnFeCoNi.
Without an applied magnetic field, the differences between CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi will remain observable but will be less pronounced.
CrMnFeCoNi has lower magnetic tunability than CrCoNi.
CrMnFeCoNi has a lower propensity for deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation than CrCoNi under matched conditions.
The proposed mechanism is limited to initially single-phase FCC alloys and to temperature, strain-rate, and magnetic-field regimes in which magnetic effects and phase transformation are active.
Dislocation density and grain-boundary effects may also contribute to the mechanical-property differences.
Failure to observe statistically significant increases in both HCP fraction and work-hardening rate in CrCoNi relative to CrMnFeCoNi under an applied field would falsify the hypothesis.
